articles.title: NASA Launches Its Most Powerful Space Telescope Today
articles.summary: Today, NASA sent a brand-new space telescope into the sky called the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope. It launched from Kennedy Space Center in Florida on a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket. The Roman Telescope has a mirror as wide as the famous Hubble Space Telescope, but it can take pictures of a much larger area of the sky — up to 100 times more in a single shot. Scientists hope it will discover around 100,000 new planets and unlock secrets about dark matter and dark energy. After launch, the telescope will travel for over three months to reach its final position about one million miles from Earth.

lv1: What is the name of the new telescope that NASA launched today? (今天NASA發射的新望遠鏡叫什麼名字？)
Which rocket carried the Roman Space Telescope into space? (哪枚火箭把羅曼太空望遠鏡送入太空？)
lv2: Why do scientists say the Roman Telescope is better than the Hubble Space Telescope for surveying the sky? (科學家為什麼說羅曼望遠鏡在巡天方面比哈勃太空望遠鏡更出色？)
What is dark matter, and why might it be important for scientists to learn more about it? (什麼是暗物質？科學家為什麼想更深入了解它？)
lv3: Space exploration costs billions of dollars. Do you think governments should keep spending money on projects like the Roman Telescope, or should that money be used to solve problems on Earth first? Give reasons for your view. (太空探索耗資數十億元。你認為政府應繼續投資羅曼望遠鏡這類項目，還是應先把資金用於解決地球上的問題？請說明你的理由。)

If the Roman Telescope discovers thousands of planets that could support life, how do you think that would change the way humans think about their place in the universe? (如果羅曼望遠鏡發現數千顆可能存在生命的星球，你認為這將如何改變人類對自身在宇宙中位置的看法？)

articles.title: Asia's Freshwater Supply Is Running Out Faster Than Expected
articles.summary: A region in Asia sometimes called the 'Asian Water Tower' — which includes the high mountains of the Himalayas and Tibetan Plateau — is losing about 24 billion tonnes of underground water every year. This water is used by hundreds of millions of people for drinking, farming, and daily life. Scientists warn that melting glaciers may give some relief around the 2060s, but unless people change how they use water, the problem will become much worse in the future. Researchers are urging governments across Asia to act now to manage water resources more carefully before the crisis becomes too serious to fix.

lv1: What nickname do scientists give to the water-rich mountain region in Asia? (科學家給亞洲這個富水山區起了什麼綽號？)
About how many billion tonnes of underground water does the Asian Water Tower lose every year? (亞洲水塔每年大約流失多少億噸地下水？)
lv2: Why might melting glaciers help with the water shortage problem for a short time, but not solve it in the long run? (為什麼冰川融化在短期內可能緩解缺水問題，但長遠來說卻無法解決問題？)
How can people's daily habits — such as farming methods and water usage — make the groundwater crisis worse or better? (人們日常習慣（如耕作方式和用水量）如何令地下水危機惡化或改善？)
lv3: When a shared water supply that crosses many countries starts to run out, who should be responsible for managing it — individual countries, or an international organisation? What challenges might each approach face? (當跨越多個國家的共同水資源開始枯竭時，應由各國自行管理，還是由國際組織負責？每種做法各有什麼挑戰？)

Some farmers depend on large amounts of water to grow enough food for their families. Is it fair to ask them to use less water to help save the environment? How might society support them while also protecting the water supply? (部分農民需要大量用水才能種出足夠糧食。要求他們節水以保護環境，這樣公平嗎？社會應如何支援他們，同時保護水資源？)

articles.title: 韓國全民免費享用AI：政府推國家級人工智能計劃
articles.summary: 韓國政府宣布推行全國性人工智能計劃，讓所有國民免費享用無限量生成式AI服務。此舉旨在減少對中美兩國AI模型的過度依賴，同時提升本國的科技競爭力。生成式AI能夠協助用戶撰寫文章、製作圖像及回答問題。專家認為，此計劃有助培養國民的數碼能力，令更多人從小接觸及學習AI技術，推動韓國在全球科技競賽中佔據更有利的地位。

lv1: 韓國政府為市民提供哪種免費服務？
韓國推出此計劃的原因之一，是希望減少依賴哪兩個國家的AI模型？
lv2: 什麼是「生成式AI」？它可以幫助我們做哪些事情？
韓國政府為何要自行研發AI服務，而不繼續使用外國的AI產品？
lv3: 如果所有市民都能免費使用強大的AI服務，你認為這對社會有哪些好處和壞處？學生會否因此變得過度依賴AI而減少獨立思考？
政府主導的AI計劃與私人科技公司研發的AI有什麼分別？你認為哪種方式對普通市民更有保障？請說明理由。

articles.title: 中尼邊境爆發嚴重泥石流　罹難失蹤人數逾三千
articles.summary: 中國與尼泊爾接壤的邊境地區近日爆發嚴重泥石流，滾滾山泥順山谷傾瀉而下，造成兩地大規模破壞。據報道，截至目前死亡及失蹤人數合共逾三千人，情況十分嚴峻。救援隊伍以「水陸空」三路並進的方式展開搜救行動，趕赴西藏日喀則市吉隆口岸一帶協助受困居民。當地橋樑及建築物受損嚴重，令救援工作困難重重。當局呼籲各界密切關注氣象變化，以防災情進一步惡化。

lv1: 這次泥石流發生在哪兩個國家的邊境附近？
救援隊伍以哪三種方式展開搜救行動？
lv2: 為什麼山區的泥石流往往比平地的水災更難救援？
橋樑和道路受損會對救災工作帶來什麼影響？
lv3: 面對日益頻繁的極端天氣和自然災害，政府和社會應如何在事前做好防災準備，而不是僅靠事後救援？
當自然災害波及兩個或以上的國家時，各國應如何合作救災？在國際救援中可能出現哪些困難或矛盾？
